items.sefariaRef: Talmud Eser HaSefirot, Section IV, List of Answers on Topics 47:1
items.html: For the illumination of the upper one that reaches the lower one is considered by it to be one degree higher than its own discernment. If it is in the discernment of Nefesh, the illumination that it receives is considered by it to be the discernment of Ruach; and if it is itself the discernment of Ruach, the illumination is considered by it to be the discernment of Neshama, and so forth. And the illumination that it receives from the upper one of its upper one is considered by it to be two degrees higher than its own discernment: if it is the discernment of Nefesh, the illumination is considered by it to be Neshama; and if it is itself Ruach, the illumination is considered by it to be the discernment of Haya, and so forth. Therefore here, where ZA is the discernment of Nefesh, the illumination that it receives from Bina is considered by it to be Ruach, she being its upper one; and the illumination that it receives from the upper one of its upper one, that is, from Hochma, is considered by it to be Neshama, and so forth in this way.
